Nov 20 : Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca has dismissed suggestions that uncertainty over the club's possible punishment for breaches of Premier League financial rules is behind his side's recent slump in form. City opened the season with seven successive league victories but head into Saturday's home clash with Fulham on the back of three straight defeats before the international break, leaving them third in the table, six points behind Arsenal. An independent commission in September found City guilty of 114 of the 115 financial charges brought by the Premier League. The club have denied wrongdoing and are appealing against the verdict. No sanction has yet been imposed but a substantial points deduction could even result in relegation, prompting questions over whether the off-field uncertainty has affected the players.

"I don't think the players are thinking too much about that," Maresca told a press conference on Friday. "If we want to relate the noise with the defeat, (Aston) Villa away we had so many chances - for instance, Iliman (Ndiaye) hit the post - Brighton their keeper was man of the match, at (Nottingham) Forest where Erling (Haaland) had the chance to score (to make it) 2-2. "I don't think the players are focused on the noise." Even without any potential punishment, City are already in danger of losing touch with champions Arsenal who have won nine of their opening 10 games. NO NEED TO PANIC Maresca, however, is not about to panic and rip up the script, insisting there is not much difference between the side that opened the season in superb fashion and the one that has suffered three defeats on the spin. "This morning they told me that we played 16 official games and we won 12... So, if in the next 16 games, you say to me that we are going to win 12, I'll sign," he said. "I was not thinking we were doing everything well when we were winning games. I'm not thinking we did everything wrong when we lost games," the Italian said. Improving a defence that has leaked eight goals in the last four league games is a priority though. "We also need to analyse the defeats. Aston Villa and Brighton, in both games man of the match was the keeper for them. At Forest we were not good enough, particularly in the first half," Maresca said. "We are conceding too many goals. Most of them are avoidable. The idea is to continue to attack in the same way, creating chances, but creating a balance when we defend." City will be boosted by the availability of defender Marc Guehi who, according to Maresca, missed England's Nations League games because of a "small issue".

Source: Reuters

WASHINGTON, Nov 20 : A founder of the artificial intelligence giant Anthropic will make a large gift to cradle-to-adulthood investment program, Trump Accounts, in the coming weeks, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said in an interview with CNBC on Friday. Anthropic raised $93.5 billion in its blockbuster IPO on Thursday after underwriters exercised an option to buy additional shares "One of the Anthropic founders is going to make a large gift to Trump Accounts over the next few weeks," Bessent said. "We believe that it's important for these great entrepreneurs to share their bounty." Trump Accounts, which will provide U.S. citizens born between 2025 and 2028 a government-funded investment account of $1,000 that families can build on, is aimed at promoting investing and financial literacy from an early age.

Source: Reuters

Nov 20 : Bitcoin, the world's largest cryptocurrency, fell below the $60,000 level on Friday for the first time since July, as lofty valuation concerns weighed on the AI trade and other risk assets.  Bitcoin was last down 3.45 per cent at $59,381. Ether, the second-largest cryptocurrency, was down 5.23 per cent at $1,648.91. Crypto markets have been shaken in recent sessions by weeks of concern about the profitability of massive AI infrastructure spending, rising borrowing costs, regulatory risks following Democrats' win in the US midterm elections and Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's departure. The main US stock indexes were on track for their steepest weekly decline since April 2025, when US President Donald Trump announced Liberation Day tariffs.

Source: Reuters

FAST

MANCHESTER, England, Nov 20 : Mauricio Pochettino pledged to rebuild Manchester United "from scratch" and urged his players to forget the club's troubled recent past ahead of a daunting first assignment at Liverpool on Sunday. The Argentine, appointed after United's difficult start to the season led to Michael Carrick's sacking, struck an upbeat tone on Friday in his first press conference as manager, saying his focus was firmly on establishing a new identity rather than dwelling on previous failures. "We arrive with the idea to create something from scratch, from our own ideas and philosophy in the way that we love to work," Pochettino said, glancing at assistant coach Jesus Perez who attended the press conference. "It is about building our own way here. The past is not going to help, to think about yesterday.

"We feel the support and we are going to work really hard to help the players to perform. That is the priority." Pochettino's first days in the job have been hectic. He left the United States in the early hours of Wednesday and began meetings with players and staff immediately. Asked about his initial objective, he smiled and said "sleep". SCALE OF THE TASK There will be little time for rest, however, with United travelling to Anfield to face Liverpool. The trip offers an immediate measure of the scale of the task confronting Pochettino as he attempts to revive a side whose confidence has been eroded by poor results. United are languishing in 18th in their worst start to a top-flight campaign in 40 years. "It is normal when you don't win games that the confidence starts to go down," he said. "I think the players need to feel from us that we believe and trust in them. "With the schedule we have ahead we have to settle on our principles. The players are intelligent, they have quality. Sometimes it is unlocking some things that didn't appear for different reasons." A key figure in any rebuilding effort will be captain Bruno Fernandes, whose future has been the subject of speculation as he has yet to agree a new deal. Pochettino revealed he had already held extensive talks with the Portugal midfielder and indicated he remained central to his plans. "Bruno is our captain and a very important player but other players have to feel they are important from the bottom to the top," he said. "We spoke (on Thursday), I spent three hours chatting with all the players individually. It was very nice contact." FITNESS AND RECRUITMENT Questions about the squad's fitness levels have swirled around Old Trafford, but Pochettino refused to criticise what he had inherited. "It is about proposing that idea to be brave and take it to the field," he said. "We cannot talk about data without context. It is easy to manipulate data but we need to be honest, sometimes they don't show something that you can see on the field. "We are here not to denounce things. We are here to build something with our players." Pochettino also made clear he expects to have a voice in recruitment and wider football matters, while accepting responsibility for results. "I was in all my career a coach, head coach, manager. It does not change too much," he said. "I know as head coach I am the guy who tomorrow will decide the squad for Sunday, pick the 11, make the changes. "I know in the future I would like to be involved in all the main decisions that affect the squad." Pochettino said he relished returning to the daily routine of club football after he led the Americans to the 2025 Gold Cup final and steered them to the last 16 of the World Cup this year on home soil. "We were missing it a lot," he said of club football. "We are animals of the grass, we like to feel the grass, to smell the grass, improve players every day."

Source: Reuters

FAST

Nov 20 : Nvidia, the centerpiece of Wall Street's AI trade, slipped behind Google parent Alphabet to become the fourth-most valuable US company on Friday, as a prolonged selloff in the chipmaker's shares reshuffled the top of the market-value rankings. The stock, last down 3 per cent and valued at $3.4 trillion, was on course for a seventh straight weekly decline, its longest losing streak since 2008. The slide comes days after Nvidia's first earnings report since co-founder Jensen Huang's resignation, which failed to ease investor concerns about leadership and the durability of AI spending. Nvidia's fall down the market-value rankings also underscores a shift within the AI trade, as investors gravitate toward companies that pair heavy AI investment with established cloud and software revenue streams. Apple, seen as less exposed to the AI trade, remained well ahead with a market value of $5.08 trillion. Microsoft ranked second at $3.72 trillion, followed by Alphabet at $3.44 trillion, according to LSEG data.

Source: Reuters

LAS VEGAS, Nov 20 : Formula One stakeholders have agreed in principle a switch away from the current crop of V6 hybrid engines to louder V8s from 2030, team bosses said ahead of the Las Vegas Grand Prix. McLaren's Zak Brown said it was now a matter of dotting the i's and crossing the t's, and Alpine's de facto team principal Flavio Briatore agreed. "We have the agreement, basically. It's not signed, but it looks like everybody's agreed to 2030 V8s," said Italian Briatore. "I think it's the right way to go. We need an engine with a lot of noise, and a simple engine, and we need to be racing with that because, in the end, I believe the best for the spectator, for everybody is a very simple engine, a lot of noise and basta (enough)."

Nov 20 : Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola wants his side to be prepared for surprises when Manchester United, under new boss Mauricio Pochettino, visit Anfield in the Premier League on Sunday. United, a lowly 18th in the table, are winless in the league since August, but Iraola believes the rivalry with Liverpool and the arrival of a new manager could breathe new life into their lacklustre campaign. "We have to acknowledge the importance of the game... they have a new manager, new challenges for us," Iraola told a press conference on Friday. "It's true that they have this small advantage, we don't have references to prepare, because they can go different ways that we honestly don't know right now."

Iraola said United's players would try to impress the new manager and that Liverpool would have to deal with that early in the game. "The beginning of the game will be important... we know their players very well, who they are, the strengths and weaknesses they have shown," the Spaniard said. Liverpool are fourth in the league and have won six of their last eight matches in all competitions, including their penalty shootout victory over Chelsea in the League Cup. Their home form continues to bother Iraola, however, with the team winning only one of their five league games at Anfield. United have not lost to rivals Liverpool since September 2024, and they have not been beaten at Anfield since a famous 7-0 thrashing by Juergen Klopp's side in March 2023. "Yes, I think we are conscious our away stats are much better. We need to improve this and United is the first chance," Iraola said. Liverpool will be boosted by the return of injured trio Jeremie Frimpong, Ryan Gravenberch and Virgil van Dijk, who should be available for Sunday's match. Giovanni Leoni and Conor Bradley have returned to training but are not yet available, Iraola added. IRAOLA CONDEMNS DRONE FILMING Iraola said he had been sent the training footage of United that a drone operator filmed this week and posted on his YouTube channel. The operator has since apologised and taken down the footage. "Yesterday they were sending me the footage. But the important part of this is, it shouldn't be legal. It happened to United but it could happen to me, to any training," Iraola said. "It's not a matter of advantage, it's the fact that someone can do this. There is a reason we train behind closed doors... I don't think it's nice for any club."

Source: Reuters

TURIN, Italy, Nov 20 : Seven-times Grand Slam champion Carlos Alcaraz eased concerns about a hamstring injury by cruising past Italian fifth seed Flavio Cobolli 6-4 6-1 in his final ATP Finals round-robin match in Turin on Friday, completing an unbeaten group-stage campaign and securing momentum ahead of the semi-finals. The Spaniard had already booked his place in the last four after victories over American seventh seed Frances Tiafoe and 2020 ATP Finals champion Daniil Medvedev, but his fitness came under scrutiny after he left the court with heavy strapping on his left leg following Wednesday's win over the Russian. Any doubts were quickly dispelled as Alcaraz broke the already-eliminated Cobolli in the opening game and surged into a 2-0 lead. The 23-year-old delivered an efficient display, keeping rallies short and dictating play without putting unnecessary strain on his body. He carried that momentum into the second set, breaking for a 2-0 lead and again to move 4-1 ahead before closing out a 65-minute victory. Alcaraz finished with 29 winners to Cobolli's nine.

"I tried to play as aggressively as I can, hit the ball as hard as I can. "The way I felt on court today was incredible. I am getting more confident after every match and hopefully I can keep it going." Alcaraz underwent an MRI scan on his left hamstring on Thursday, with Spanish media reporting that the examination ruled out a serious injury. He also cancelled a practice session that day and delayed his scheduled warm-up from 1045 to 1300 local time earlier on Friday. While the convincing win eased immediate concerns over his availability for the knockout stage, the defending Australian Open champion will continue to manage the issue as the season-ending tournament reaches its decisive phase. Alcaraz is enjoying a resurgent end to the year after spending more than four months sidelined with a wrist injury sustained at the ATP 500 event in Barcelona. Since returning at the US Open in September, where he was beaten by Ben Shelton in the quarter-finals, Alcaraz has claimed titles in Tokyo, Vienna and Paris to re-establish himself among the favourites for the season-ending crown. With three wins from three in the Ivan Lendl group, Alcaraz heads into the semi-final against American third seed Shelton in strong form as he bids to capture his first ATP Finals title. Five-times Grand Slam champion Jannik Sinner has already ended his season because of a persistent knee injury, while world number one Alexander Zverev remains among the leading contenders in Turin.

Nov 19 : Bertelsmann has no plan to enter the video games market despite the blockbuster success of "Grand Theft Auto VI," said Thomas Rabe, CEO of the German media group that published the original game in the franchise. Huge global demand for GTA VI is expected to generate revenue far exceeding its estimated development costs of around $1 billion. But "not every game becomes as successful as GTA," Rabe said and cautioned that gaming remains a hit-driven business, similar to the film industry. "New games are not easy to establish." Bertelsmann's BMG Interactive division published the first "Grand Theft Auto" in 1997. The next year, the company sold the business to Take-Two Interactive, which went on to develop one of the world's most successful gaming franchises. Rabe said his company has repeatedly examined entering the gaming market over the past 10 to 15 years, but decided against it. He cited high acquisition costs, reputational risks and the industry's reliance on a few blockbusters. Bertelsmann, whose businesses include broadcaster RTL Group, publisher Penguin Random House, music company BMG and logistics provider Arvato, sees little need to expand into other sectors, Rabe said.

Source: Reuters

Nov 20 : South Africa captain Siya Kolisi hit back at a suggestion Springbok coach Rassie Erasmus was being "dramatic" in saying the side had let the country down in defeat by France as the team vowed they would not be sidetracked by the latter's suspension. Erasmus made the statement on Monday in announcing his team for the Nations Championship clash with Ireland in Dublin on Saturday, the same press conference from which he received a six-match ban from World Rugby for criticising the match officials in Paris. Kolisi was asked if the coach was being dramatic with the statement, a suggestion which clearly riled the Springbok captain. "Did you say it was dramatic?" he asked twice. Nov 20 : Grand Theft Auto, banned in Saudi Arabia until last year, is now being embraced not only by its gamers - a category that includes Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman - but also by its sovereign wealth fund, which the prince chairs. This week, gamers in Saudi Arabia joined legions of fans around the world to play Grand Theft Auto VI upon launch — the first new release of the top-selling series since a Saudi ban was scrapped in 2025. "Playing GTA VI in Saudi Arabia legally makes me so happy, because we're talking about a game that was banned," local content creator Thamer al Dairem said from a windowless, air-conditioned room, lit mostly by the bank of monitors displaying the game. "We're talking about the biggest game in the world."

Support and investment in gaming by Saudi Arabia have been rising fast, not least from de facto ruler Mohammed bin Salman, often known by his initials MBS, who told Fox News in 2023 that gaming helped him disconnect and let off steam. The Public Investment Fund (PIF), the sovereign wealth fund he chairs, owns a major stake worth over $2 billion in Take-Two Interactive, the US firm that owns Grand Theft Auto-developer Rockstar Games, LSEG Workspace data show. CHANGING CUSTOMS IN CONSERVATIVE SAUDI ARABIA In August, a consortium including PIF acquired gaming giant Electronic Arts for $55 billion. This month, gaming software provider Unity Software held talks with investors including the Saudi sovereign wealth fund on a potential buyout valuing it at around $25 billion. PIF, which has spent the past year consolidating its gaming holdings into a subsidiary, Savvy Games Group, declined to comment. MBS has been leading a campaign to open Saudi Arabia up and ease strict social and cultural norms that revolve around a conservative interpretation of Islam — a far cry from GTA VI's Vice City. GTA VI advertisements have been appearing in some of Saudi Arabia's most popular shopping malls. One image shows the heroine wearing shorts and a crop top, her arm resting on her partner's shoulder — unthinkable a few years ago, when women were required to dress modestly and cover their hair. MBS's wider reform plan, dubbed Vision 2030, is all about reducing reliance on oil and gas revenues, both in the economy and in state revenues, and PIF strategy is part of that. "(It) is part of a diversified long-term investment strategy to capture value from industries it does not traditionally operate within," said Piers Harding-Rolls, who researches games at Ampere Analysis. In Riyadh, al Dairem is now streaming Grand Theft Auto content and says that, while some of the depictions of violence, drugs and sex are extreme, the game is age-restricted and reflects another country. "The city is Vice City, and it's representing Miami and the chaotic things that happen. For us Saudis, like, we know that it has nothing to do with us." The gaming experience, on the other hand, matters hugely to him. "When I saw the ads of GTA VI in the malls, I was so happy. If you'd asked me if I was ever going to see this, like, 10 years ago in Saudi, I wouldn't have believed it."

(Editing by Adam Jourdan and Kevin Liffey)

Nov 20 : Brighton and Hove Albion manager Fabian Huerzeler says his high-flying team must quickly re-focus as the Premier League resumes after the international break with the south coast club being billed as potential title contenders. The stoppage interrupted an incredible start to the season for Brighton who have soared into second place behind defending champions Arsenal with 22 points from 10 games. Brighton travel to Hull City on Sunday having won six of their last seven league games including a stunning 3-0 home drubbing of Arsenal and a victory at Manchester City. They are the top flight's highest scorers with 26 goals and have conceded just seven, with only Arsenal leaking fewer, and according to Opta have an 8.45 per cent chance of pulling off the most surprising title grab since Leicester City in 2016.

Huerzeler knows momentum will be key if the Seagulls are to continue soaring. "It's never easy (after the international break), but we managed it in the last period quite well and I hope we can manage it in this period as well," the German said. "For us it is very important to really get the players understanding what our principles and values are here. They all hear different tactics and formations in their national teams and now it is about us giving them an understanding about what made us strong and what will make us strong in the future." While Brighton have been free-scoring, all seven of their Premier League wins this season have come with clean sheets. Huerzeler's intense pressing style has seen Brighton make a league-leading 106 high turnovers this season while they lead the way in chances converted and goals from set plays. BASICS BEHIND BRIGHTON'S RISE At 33, Huerzeler is the youngest manager in the Premier League, and while his methods have been lauded, he says Brighton's rise is rooted in basics. "The game is evolving and I try to evolve things and adjust things. But ultimately football in the end is still like 20 years ago in terms of running, winning duels and counter pressing," he said. "I wouldn't say we innovate or that I'm doing special things. I just try to be really good in the basics and develop my players with the staff." German midfielder Pascal Gross has been a key figure this season and is finally getting the recognition he deserves with four goals and four assists in the Premier League. He is set for his 300th appearance on Sunday. "He gives everyone an understanding of what it means to be successful. He's a great standard and culture driver. That's his biggest impact," Huerzeler said. Brighton will still be without Stefanos Tzimas, who is back in training after an ACL injury, while Japan winger Kaoru Mitoma is still "one or two weeks" from a return. Nigeria forward Zadok Yohanna will miss the Hull trip with a hamstring injury.

Nov 20 : Southampton coach Tonda Eckert has signed a new contract through 2029, the second-tier club said on Friday, despite uncertainty over his future following his role in the "spygate" scandal. Eckert was handed a suspended six-week ban and fined £28,000 ($36,697) after admitting he authorised the observation of training sessions involving three rival Championship clubs last season. The Football Association charged Eckert in July, with an independent regulatory commission imposing the sanctions after a hearing. The governing body confirmed in October that the ban would remain suspended until the end of the 2027-28 season. "We've had some conversations that started a couple of weeks ago, and the goal was always clear: to show the same commitment we have had for the last 12 months," Eckert told the club website.

"I am very grateful for that. We have started a journey that is not even halfway through - there is a lot more to come." Eckert guided Southampton from 21st place to a fourth-placed finish last season. However, the club were thrown out of the Championship playoff final and docked four points for the 2026-27 campaign over the "spygate" affair. Southampton, who are seventh in the Championship standings, host Derby County on Saturday. ($1 = 0.7630 pounds)
